message: rebuild-from-events now lands db.sqlite at the CURRENT schema version: rebuildReadModelFromEvents (src/compact.js) stamps the 0.5 floor then runs migrate({quiet:true}) once inside the rebuild. Root cause of the post-compaction noise: writeViewSqlite builds the post-v0.7 shape but the stamp said 0.5, so EVERY next read re-ran and re-announced v0.6/v0.7. Merge 5a286a0; regression test test/rebuild-schema-current.test.js.

PATTERN: any code path that rewrites db.sqlite wholesale (writeViewSqlite targets) must bring it to the current schema version via migrate(db, {quiet:true}) — never hardcode a version number; the chain owns 'current' so a future v0.8 data backfill runs at rebuild time too.

check.js checkEntries: the store's OWN repoRoot gets the same src/-shorthand fallback as entry-named external roots (shared withSrc helper). Was a standing false positive: loom entries cite capabilities/queue.ts for src/capabilities/queue.ts and doctor flagged them missing (3 of the 2026-07-12 loom triage candidates). Merge 194c339.

atomicityOf (src/rubric.js) exempts messages with the '[rollup] ' prefix — a compaction rollup is multi-fact by construction, and doctor's non-atomic detector was telling the operator to split what compact just joined (3 loom triage candidates were the store's own rollups). Exemption sits in the ONE shared predicate so doctor, log --strict, and the atomicity scoreboard all agree. Merge e5a4130.

generateRollupMessage dedupes exact-duplicate source messages (Set, first-seen order) — a runaway logger had appended one fact 45x to the loom store and the rollup text would have repeated it 45 times. All duplicate eids still land in the supersede's rolls_up; only the TEXT collapses. Near-duplicate REWORDINGS are NOT merged (semantic dedup is an LLM job, out of pebbl's deterministic scope). Merge 9b778b2.

Loom-store triage 2026-07-12: 45 identical live entries (t-6bb26ff4 collision-guard note) were appended by an external runaway logger on the loom side, 17:54-20:01Z in ~2s bursts — NOT a pebbl bug (each was a real pebbl log call; db+event pairs consistent). A write-time exact-duplicate advisory in log.js could catch this shape early; not built yet.

Fresh 'pebbl init' prints the v0.4..v0.7 migration lines on a brand-new store: db.js SCHEMA stamps the 0.3 floor and openDb's migrate() announces the climb. Cosmetic and once-only (unlike the fixed post-rebuild re-run) but the same alarming-noise family; candidate follow-up is to stamp a fresh store at current silently.

Scanner false positive, second occurrence: the [cred-path] rule fired on the dot-env suffix inside an ordinary JS/TS environment-property access (this time in jig tracers/11-canvas token-picker.spec.ts; first time was the spike-6 DTCG token strings that led to the stashed unauthorized scanner edit). Builders keep contorting code (bracket notation) to dodge it, which is worse than the false positive. Proposed fix for Ashley's review: exempt the exact language idioms for reading environment variables - they are language idioms, not file paths.

handoff now REFUSES a detail-heavy handoff (>1200 chars of done+todo+blocked) that links neither --docs nor --no-doc — a write-time guard in handoff.js that fails BEFORE the insert, like malformedSummary. Because detail was either crammed into the fields (an unsearchable wall) or written to an orphaned unlinked doc, so the readable 'rendered document' got produced only a fraction of the time. --no-doc is the explicit escape hatch so a long-but-terse handoff is never forced to truncate its own content. Also: context.js resurfaces linked docs on pickup (were invisible before), and --docs/--no-doc are documented in help + the installed AGENTS block. Landed main 1dec3dc.

fix(privacy-scan): narrow three false-positive families in the scanner

Fixed three scanner false-positive families in src/privacy-scan.js (commit 88c12d9, merge of fix/scanner-false-positives). (1) DTCG design-token paths: assignment-quoted/bare patterns were tripping on JSON schema entries like { "token": "color.primary" } because 'token' is an ASSIGNMENT_KEYWORD and the value is 12+ chars. Added DTCG_TOKEN_PATH_RE and skip captured values matching it in findTokens. Structural exemption, not a keyword allowlist - dot-notation identifiers are too narrow to be real secrets. (2) Language idioms for reading environment variables: CRED_PATH_PATTERNS[1] was matching property chains that contain neither a slash nor a hyphen. Tightened to require one of those in the matched token, so genuine hyphenated credential filenames and dotfile env paths under a directory still fire while the language idioms no longer do; the bare basename and the /root credential-dir shapes stay covered by patterns[0] and [2]. The exact regexes live in src/privacy-scan.js and are deliberately NOT copied here - a regex quoted in prose drifts from the one that runs, and quoting cred-path patterns makes the memory itself unpublishable. (3) Template placeholders fire and are intentionally left firing - a placeholder is ambiguous because it could expand to a real secret at runtime. Added 15 test fixtures to test/privacy-scan.test.js covering all three families. Full suite 605/0. Supersedes stash@{0} 'UNAUTHORIZED subagent edit 2026-07-28' (dropped after merge).

rubric migrations can now ADD a missing rule, not only edit an existing one: added the v0.7 step that inserts the steering rule when absent. The v0.5/v0.6 steps only rewrote a steering/correction rule that was already present, so 6 stores whose rubric.yml predated that rule (lumr, lief, Butterfly-Guide, Market-Analyzer, security, the Documents pebbl clone) never gained it — friction/regression/parked entries there fell through to no match and needed a manual --cat forever. Upgrade was reporting 'rubric.yml already up to date' over the gap, which is why it went unnoticed across a full 17-repo rollout.

the v0.4 ^trace: insertion anchored on the literal text [session], which never matches a rubric whose pattern is escaped as ^\[session\] — indexOf returned -1, the insert point collapsed to the first blank line, and the rule was written ABOVE the rules: key. pebbl's lenient hand-rolled parser reads such a rule anyway, so nothing broke visibly and 4 stores carried invalid YAML that any real parser would reject. Fixed by anchoring every insertion through insertRule (always below rules:, and below the [session] rule so it keeps first-match) plus a v0.8 repair step that moves stray rules back under the key.

rule ORDER is load-bearing in rubric.yml and insertions must respect it: the [session] rule has to stay above the unanchored keyword rules, or a session dump merely mentioning 'regression' classifies as steering instead of staying fleeting. First-match-wins makes any insertion anchor a behavioural decision, not a formatting one — my first pass at the v0.7 fix inserted correctly-shaped rules in the wrong position and demoted [session] in 4 stores before the anchor was fixed and the stores re-migrated.

pebbl's first-two-months memory (125 entries, 2026-05-23 to 2026-07-02) was orphaned in a second clone at ~/Documents/10.Code-Projects/pebbl and nearly deleted with it. The live repo moved to ~/pebbl on 2026-06-24 and started a FRESH store, so the live store only went back to 2026-07-12 — a 10-day gap hid the fact that the tool's own design rationale (sentinel-block choice, PEBBL.md retirement, storage/search/compaction/rubric/handoff decisions) lived nowhere else. Rescued to the dev-tools repo at ~/Documents/10.Code-Projects/dev-tools/pebbl-history/store; the clone is deleted and its one unique commit (loom routing in AGENTS.md) cherry-picked here. Lesson: relocating a repo silently orphans its store — a clone move needs the .pebbl to come with it.

pebbl's own live store now lives in the dev-tools repo (dev-tools/pebbl-history/live) with ~/pebbl/.pebbl symlinked to it. It was gitignored here — 0 tracked files — so every decision we logged about pebbl was unversioned and one disk failure from gone, the same failure that orphaned the first 125 entries in the abandoned clone. Symlink verified end to end first: reads, writes, and post-commit capture all work through it because find-pebbl uses statSync, which follows symlinks. The .gitignore entry stays so the symlink itself is never committed here.

no duplicates left on this machine: the npm global pebbl was a dangling symlink to the deleted ~/Documents/pebbl, so 'npm ls -g' claimed pebbl was installed while the only working entry point was ~/bin/pebbl -> ~/pebbl/bin/pebbl.js. Removed it. A dead duplicate is worse than none: it resolves on PATH order, not on which copy is real.
verifying the daily memory-commit script end to end: this entry should be committed by bin/commit-memory.sh with the privacy scan passing, not by hand.

launchd cannot exec a script inside ~/Documents: macOS TCC protects Documents/Desktop/Downloads, so a user agent pointed straight at a script there dies with 'Operation not permitted' before the script runs. Fix is a one-line shim in ~/bin that execs the real script; the digests job never hit this because ~/digests is outside the protected set.

dev-tools moved from ~/Documents/10.Code-Projects to ~/dev-tools because macOS TCC gives launchd agents zero access to Documents (read dir, read file, git status all DENIED — proved with a probe agent). Matches loom, pebbl and digests, which already live at home root for the same reason; the alternative was granting Full Disk Access to /bin/bash, which would hand every bash script on the machine full disk access. Ten symlinks repointed.
final verification: this entry exists to prove the launchd job commits pebbl memory unattended from ~/dev-tools, privacy scan included.
instrumented the dev-tools memory pipeline against silent failure: 8 invariant checks + a pebbl liveness heartbeat beaten only on verified success, so loom maintain escalates an absent beat every 4h.
